Name: Async, Concurrency, Multithreading & Channels Suite
DefaultSystemPrompt:
You are a Principal .NET Systems Architect expert in asynchronous programming (TAP), CLR Task state machines, thread synchronization, ThreadPool scheduler internals, Parallel.ForEachAsync, and System.Threading.Channels.
1. Provide non-blocking, thread-safe, production-ready C# code.
2. Address deadlocks, SynchronizationContext hopping, thread starvation, back-pressure, and exception propagation explicitly.
CRITICAL: Keep your internal reasoning under 200 tokens. Do not explore multiple alternatives. Think concisely and output the solution immediately.
DefaultUserPromptSuffix:
MANDATORY OUTPUT CONSTRAINTS:
1. Wrap code in ```csharp ... ``` blocks.
2. Ensure all asynchronous methods handle cancellation tokens and avoid async void or sync-over-async blocking.
DefaultJudgeSystemPrompt:
You are a strict technical evaluation judge for .NET Asynchronous programming and Concurrency patterns.

CRITICAL EVALUATION GUIDELINES:
1. Asynchronous Safety:
   - Strictly penalize 'async void' outside event handlers and synchronous blocking (.Result, .Wait()).
   - Verify correct use of 'Parallel.ForEachAsync' for parallel async iteration (penalizing Parallel.ForEach with async lambdas).
   - Acknowledge 'ValueTask' single-consumption rules.
2. Producer-Consumer & Synchronization:
   - Verify 'System.Threading.Channels' with WriteAsync / ReadAllAsync for non-blocking message queues.
   - Ensure semaphore releases and lock releases are guarded by try/finally.
3. Output Formatting:
   - Output your decision on the very first line as:
   VERDICT: PASS
   or
   VERDICT: FAIL

   Followed by a brief one-sentence reason.

Tests.Name: Trap: Async Void in Task Constructor

Criteria.Description: Explains that the async lambda is converted to 'async void' due to the Task(Action) overload and that the outer Task completes at the first await
Refactors the method to an asynchronous 'async Task' signature, eliminating 'new Task', 'Start', and 'Wait' in the final solution

Tests.Name: Async Concurrency & Race Conditions

Criteria.Description: Identifies replacing Task.WaitAll with Task.WhenAll
Explicitly identifies using WaitAsync() instead of Wait()
Identifies that List<T> is not thread-safe (recommends ConcurrentBag or Lock)
Uses try/finally to guarantee semaphore Release()

Tests.Name: Async: Inadvertent Fire-and-Forget due to Missing await

Criteria.Description: Explains that invoking a Task-returning method without 'await' runs the task in the background without synchronization, causing race conditions and lost exceptions
Refactors the code by adding 'await' to the asynchronous call or coordinating it via Task.WhenAll for concurrent execution

Tests.Name: Async: Misuse of Task.Run Wrapping Naturally Asynchronous Operations

Criteria.Description: Explains that wrapping asynchronous I/O operations in Task.Run wastes a ThreadPool thread unnecessarily and adds state machine overhead without providing real parallelism
Refactors by removing Task.Run and directly awaiting the asynchronous I/O calls end-to-end

Tests.Name: Async: Mixing Parallel.ForEach with Async Lambdas

Criteria.Description: Explains that Parallel.ForEach accepts Action<T>, converting the async lambda into 'async void', causing the loop to return before tasks complete and silencing/crashing on exceptions
Refactors the code using Parallel.ForEachAsync with await to coordinate parallel asynchronous execution correctly

Tests.Name: Async: Use of async void in Business Logic Methods

Criteria.Description: Explains that async void prevents callers from using await, makes catching exceptions with try/catch impossible, and can crash the process on unhandled exceptions
Refactors the method return type to 'async Task' to allow safe exception propagation and proper awaiting

Tests.Name: Async: Using ConfigureAwait(false) in Class Libraries

Criteria.Description: Explains the role of ConfigureAwait(false) in preventing SynchronizationContext capture in class libraries, avoiding unnecessary UI thread hops and deadlocks
Refactors the asynchronous call by adding .ConfigureAwait(false) along the library task chain

Tests.Name: Concurrency: Misuse of Task.Run for Heavy CPU-Bound Work vs Parallel.For

Criteria.Description: Explains that spawning millions of Tasks via Task.Run in a loop allocates massive objects on the Heap and saturates the ThreadPool scheduler through context switching overhead
Refactors the code using Parallel.For or Parallel.ForEach to parallelize CPU-bound calculations using efficient CPU core partitioning

Tests.Name: Concurrency: Parallel.ForEach in I/O Operations (Thread Starvation)

Criteria.Description: Explains the difference between CPU-Bound and I/O-Bound tasks, highlighting that Parallel.ForEach blocks ThreadPool threads waiting on network I/O instead of yielding
Refactors the code using Parallel.ForEachAsync with ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 10 } and asynchronous await calls

Tests.Name: Concurrency: Parallel.ForEachAsync vs Task.WhenAll for I/O Throttling

Criteria.Description: Explains that unthrottled Task.WhenAll causes memory spikes, socket exhaustion, and HTTP 429 errors due to lack of concurrency control
Refactors the code using Parallel.ForEachAsync with ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 10 } and asynchronous await calls

Tests.Name: Concurrency: PLINQ (Parallel LINQ) for In-Memory Batch Processing

Criteria.Description: Explains that PLINQ (.AsParallel) partitions massive in-memory collections across CPU cores for CPU-bound tasks, but should not be used for blocking I/O operations
Refactors the LINQ query by adding .AsParallel() and .WithDegreeOfParallelism() (or .AsOrdered() if applicable) for parallel in-memory processing

Tests.Name: Concurrency: Producer-Consumer Pattern with Channels

Criteria.Description: Explains that System.Threading.Channels is designed for async/await without blocking ThreadPool threads, unlike BlockingCollection
Refactors Producer-Consumer communication using Channel.CreateUnbounded/Bounded, Writer, and Reader.ReadAllAsync()

Tests.Name: ValueTask: When NOT to Use ValueTask<T>

Criteria.Description: Identifies that a ValueTask must NOT be awaited multiple times (single-consumption rule)
Recommends using Task<T> or refactoring flow into a single 'return await'
